subject: Why layer 29 costs 110.89 ms in a single launch, and where the fix already lives in the tree.
findings: The profile's launch counts identify the layer: 29 calls of gguf_q4_k_selected_dual_q8_1_ds4_mmq32_fused_prefill (the fused MMQ32 gate/up route) against 1 call of gguf_q5_k_selected_grouped_row4_bf16_kernel at 110.89 ms. Gemma 4 26B-A4B's MoE layers are architecturally uniform, so the one q5_k layer is a quant difference, not a shape difference, and its gate_up costs about 17x what a q4_k layer's does (110.89 against 189.24/29 = 6.53 ms).

The gate is in gemma4_project_experts_gate_up_mmq, which returns False unless weight.spec.quant_key == 'gguf_q4_k'. That is capability-correct rather than a defect: the q4_k route quantizes activations to DS4 Q8_1 and runs MMQ32, while the q5_k route is a different design - iu8-WMMA with a 3-plane residual int8 activation and a risk+repair pass - and its wrapper takes risk_count_ptr, risk_indices_ptr, max_risks and risk_multiplier, which the q4_k route has no equivalent of.

The fast q5_k route is already implemented and already registered. hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/quant/gguf_q5_k_q8_1_selected_prefill.py says in its own docstring that it is the production-enveloped iu8-WMMA risk+repair machinery adapted from gguf_q4_k_selected_prefill.py to Q5_K weights, and that the sparse exact repair reproduces the strict row4 parent bit-exactly. It exposes both halves: gguf_q5_k_selected_dual_wmma_iu8_risk_prefill_bf16_bf16_out and gguf_q5_k_selected_dual_sparse_exact_repair_bf16.

What is missing is the gemma4 wiring, and its size matters. The q5_k halves are not driven from a small reusable helper: their only caller is hipengine/runtime/qwen4_exp_runner.py, a Qwen-specific runner of several thousand lines that owns the risk buffers and sequences the risk pass against the sparse repair. Nothing under gemma4_experts.py reaches them, so gemma4 falls back to the strict row4 parent for the one layer whose weights are Q5_K. Mirroring it is a port of that sequencing rather than a flag flip.

size_of_the_prize.unexplained: Even after that speedup, layer 29's gate_up would sit an order of magnitude above a q4_k layer's 6.53 ms, and the 17x gap is not explained by the route difference alone. Either the 30 MoE layers do not share expert shapes, or the q4_k fused MMQ32 route is doing something the q5_k path has no equivalent of. That is a separate question and worth resolving before the port, because it decides whether the ceiling is 2% or much more.
size_of_the_prize.supersedes: An earlier revision of this artifact said the prize was about 100 ms and 5% of prefill by reading the 17x as what the fast route would recover. The measured iu8 speedup is 1.50-2.00x, so 5% is wrong and the correct figure is 1.9-2.8% unless the unexplained 17x gap has another cause.
size_of_the_prize.lower_bound_note: The 1.50-2.00x figure for the iu8 route was measured operation-complete at m=1..8, which are decode-shaped row counts. Layer 29's prefill runs at m in the hundreds. A 128-thread GEMV-style kernel with strided k ownership and a serial wave sum, which is what the row4 parent is, degrades badly as m grows, while a WMMA prefill route should not. So 1.50-2.00x is a lower bound for this use, not the expected value, and the ceiling is set by the q4_k MMQ32 number at 6.53 ms per layer. The honest range is therefore 1.9% to about 5% of prefill, and the only way to narrow it is to wire the route and measure at m=512.

limits: The 17x comparison assumes the 30 MoE layers share expert shapes. The launch counts (29 plus 1) and Gemma 4 26B-A4B's uniform MoE design support that, but the expert shapes were not read from the artifact, so treat 17x as an indication of the gap rather than a measured per-shape ratio.

This is a finding, not a change. Wiring the route is a changed-arithmetic path - the iu8 activation quantization and the sparse repair both move the arithmetic - so it needs its execution-profile gate before it can become a default, and it should land behind the same rollback lever the q4_k route uses.

prior_art.what: The iu8-WMMA + Kahan-risk + sparse pair2-exact repair route this finding proposes to wire up was measured and promoted for Qwen in this repository.
entries: 2026-09-07 candidate screen: iu8-WMMA + Kahan-risk + sparse pair2-exact repair is bit-identical to the exact pair2 parent in all 32 screen cases, and 1.50-2.00x operation-complete at m=1..8, floor misses below m=1.
2026-09-07 iu8-risk exact MoE promoted: full 12-case chunk1024 A/B, 72 exact trajectories, every prefill case improves, PP512/1024/4096 +7.602%/+8.842%/+8.361%.
prior_art.why_it_matters: Two things follow. The route is exact rather than approximate, so the gate it needs is bit-exactness against the strict row4 parent rather than a KL envelope, which makes it far cheaper to validate. And the size of the win is bounded by that 1.50-2.00x, not by the 17x the q4_k comparison suggests.

prerequisites_for_the_port.scratch: Gemma4ExpertScratch has no risk buffers; qwen4_exp_runner calls scratch.ensure_group_risk_buffers(compact_rows=..., out_features_total=...) and then memsets risk_count to zero before each layer. The gemma4 dataclass has a clean buffer(name) accessor and a size map, so this is additive.
prerequisites_for_the_port.tile_map: qwen35_moe_wmma_tile_map exists in hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/moe/group_scatter.py and is reusable as is.
prerequisites_for_the_port.sequencing_reference: hipengine/runtime/qwen4_exp_runner.py around line 3845: tile map, ensure risk buffers, memset the count, resolve the risk and repair variants by (backend, layer='moe_linear', quant=...), call the risk kernel, then the repair.
prerequisites_for_the_port.template_in_gemma4: gemma4_project_experts_gate_up_mmq is the q4_k shape to mirror: gate on quant and shapes, reuse scratch buffers, build the tile map, read back total_rows and validate it against capacity, then one fused call.

shapes_resolved.method: Parsed the GGUF tensor table of gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf directly (658 tensors, 60 metadata keys).
shapes_resolved.conclusion: The two layers have identical expert shapes and differ only in quant. The 17x is therefore entirely a kernel-route difference, and Q5_K's ~22% larger weights cannot account for it. Layer 29's ffn_down_exps is also the same shape at blk.0's (704, 2816, 128) versus blk.29's (704, 2816, 128), both type 8 (Q8_0), so the down side is quant-identical and only gate_up differs.
